answer_expect.why:
🔴 THIS EXPECTATION WAS RECALIBRATED 2026-08-23, BECAUSE THE FIX MADE THE OLD PHRASE LIE.

The original gate was none_of:['currently offer'], calibrated on the BROKEN population where that phrase only ever occurred as the false claim — 'here is what your configured providers currently offer', said over registry rows. It discriminated perfectly THEN: 9 of the 10 pre-fix replies contained it and the single reply that actually called settings_provider_inventory did not.

After the result-level `note` shipped, 4 of 5 replies still contain 'currently offer' — inside a CORRECT sentence: 'These are the models currently REGISTERED in your account. If you want the live, real-time inventory of what your providers are currently offering, let me know and I can check that for you.' The gate was red over the right answer. A phrase-level gate calibrated on the broken population marks the very distinction the fix introduces, because the fixed answer has to NAME the thing it is not, in order to disclaim it.

So the expectation now asserts the PROPOSITION rather than a symptom of its absence, and the separation was measured over both populations before it was adopted:

    'registered in your account'   pre-fix  0/10   (c3-close-raw.json, c3-run-raw.json)
                                   post-fix 5/5    (c3-note-raw.json)
    'currently offer'              pre-fix  9/10   post-fix 4/5 — no longer discriminating

D-LIVE-INVENTORY-ANSWERED-FROM-THE-REGISTRY IS FIXED and this is the evidence for it. What is still not satisfied is a DIFFERENT bar: settings_provider_inventory is called 0/5, so the model stops at a correct disclaimer and an OFFER to check live inventory instead of checking it. That is the tool-surfacing problem, and it is why this tool concludes `blocked` and not `proven`.

ship_audit.refusals: EXERCISED 2026-08-14 at the TOOL boundary with SCHEMA-VALID arguments — two of these first died in argument validation (fact_type / scope enums), which is UNPROBED rather than refused, and re-probed with valid enum values afterwards. scope=user. Called as claude-test2 with the HARNESS user's provider_credential_id: refused 'not accessible' — a credential id is not a capability.
ship_audit.gate: Tier R; returns no secrets by contract.

tools.blocked_reason:
THE SECOND HALF OF THE QUESTION IS SILENTLY DROPPED, AND THE SUPPLIER WAS ALREADY IN HAND. Surfaced 5/5, called 0/5, zero errored runs.

The prompt is two questions: 'What models can I use? Show me what my configured provider actually offers.' They have different answers, measured by calling both tools directly:
    settings_list_models         -> 18 models   (what the user has REGISTERED)
    settings_provider_inventory  -> 69 models   (what the PROVIDER offers)
On 5 of 5 runs the model called settings_list_models - three or four times - and never the inventory. So the user asked for 69 and was shown 18.

🔴 IT IS NOT A FALSE STATEMENT, AND THAT MATTERS. The tempting reading is that the model passed off the registered list as the provider's catalogue; it did not. Its own words on every run are 'You have several models REGISTERED IN YOUR ACCOUNT' / 'I can see the models you have currently registered'. The first question is answered accurately and completely. The second is never answered and never acknowledged - an incomplete answer, not a wrong one, and it must be recorded as the smaller thing it is.

NOT the depth-1 supplier defect either, and this is the diagnostic point: settings_provider_inventory requires provider_credential_id, and settings_list_models RETURNS one on every model row (verified directly - '019dc738-53b1-75ea-b5d5-6aca0eed3cd8'). The model called that supplier three or four times per run, so it held the id it needed and still did not make the call. Nothing was missing from its surface.

That places it with D-SURFACING-IS-NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICIENT-THE-MODEL-PICKS-THE-SIBLING, with one difference worth keeping: here R1 forced BOTH tools onto the wire (answerable_tools returns {settings_list_models, settings_provider_inventory} for this request), the sibling answered half the question, and the model stopped there rather than choosing wrongly. A completeness failure rather than a mis-selection.

Every other gate bar passes on this evidence, SHIP exercised included. LIVE called is the only failure, and it is the tool's whole problem.
